body:
It seems that you followed the principle of [denormalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_normalization) in your index. Algolia, and other search engines, usually use the [denormalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denormalization) strategy because they support other constraints than most databases (including high performance).

We didn't yet consider the feature you're suggesting because we'd need to make a lot of assumptions:

* Is the index name a valid-enough heuristic to "merge" the facets results?
* Should we target `n` indices every time a query is performed?
* How does this fit in the [Federated Search](https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/building-search-ui/resources/ui-and-ux-patterns/in-depth/multi-index-search/js/) paradigm?

Another solution that I would have seen and would have expected to work if I was a first-time Algolia user would be to access the images as part of the facet value schema. To my knowledge, there's no easy way to retrieve the images associated with the facet value even if you were to store the image with the refined value in the index (`{ "value": "Samsung", "image": "samsung.svg" }`). This happens because Algolia only returns the faceted value (`"Samsung"`), and not the whole object.

The easiest solution for now would be to facet the strings and to use some pattern matching in the frontend.
